# Report plan rubric, v2

This rubric scores one report plan (`report-plan/1`) against the page contract in `docs/eval-report-kit/GENERATOR.md`.
`v2.json` beside this file holds the same items as data; the two are one version and change together. A version is
immutable once committed: a change adds the next version's two files, and `DIGESTS.json` pins each file's sha256, so an
edit to a committed version fails the test that reads it.

**What changed from v1** (owner, 2026-10-25, after the blind calibration of v1 on the anchors): R4 no longer counts
Method's required entries as a second statement of a caveat; R10 accepts a decisive direction clear from context; R12
is new.

## How a plan is scored

- **R1 is scored by code**, never by a model: the plan checks (`validate_plan`) and the spine lookup in `v2.json`.
- **R2 to R12 are scored by a model judge** (or by the owner, for an anchor). Each item gets one verdict, `pass` or
  `fail`, a one-sentence reason, and a quote: text copied exactly from the plan's prose, as written (figure keys and
  all) or as rendered. A `fail` always carries a quote of the failing text; a `pass` may leave it empty where the
  item concerns something absent (no flag, no confidence clauses).
- Read the plan as a reviewer reads the page: the prose rendered with its figures, in page order, top to bottom.
- Score each item on its own. A plan can fail R2 and pass everything else.
- An item that does not apply to the plan's mode passes, and its reason says so (R7 and R10 name the tradeoff slots
  that stand in for Watch and Next).

## Items

| Id | Item | Pass when | Fail when |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Shape, mode, spine and order (code) | The plan checks pass, and the first evidence section draws its shape's spine chart. | A plan check refuses it, or the first section is not a spine chart. |
| R2 | The headline is the call | A decision (instruction and reason), a trade (both sides, where the loss sits) or a stated no-call (what is missing, what would settle it), matching `headline_kind`, agreeing with the options table and the first chart. | A restated question or topic; the wrong kind; a different option than the table's; a claim the first chart contradicts. |
| R3 | The lede | At most two sentences: the strongest supporting fact, then what would change the answer. | Longer; restates the headline; background or method; nothing on what would change the answer. |
| R4 | Each caveat once, at its level | A flag only for report-wide disclosures, saying what it weakens and what survives; every caveat said once, beside its claim or in the confidence. Method's required entries (the judge and its tier, the interval method and level, cases and repeats, the cost basis) are definitions, not a second statement. | A caveat said twice outside Method's required entries; a scoped caveat in the flag; a flag silent on what it weakens and what survives. |
| R5 | Section headlines are findings | Each section headline is a finding with subject and direction that its chart shows. | A topic label, or a claim the chart does not show. |
| R6 | Reader names above Full results | Reader words for every measure, dimension, stratum and run above Full results; trial and case ids only on example cards. | An internal id, hash, run id or measure key above Full results. |
| R7 | Watch names the weakest margin | Watch names the weakest margin under the call (or the borderline cell and the sample to settle it), then scoped confounds or unmeasured risks. In tradeoff mode, Where the answer flips names the flip point. | Generic monitoring advice; caveats only; a margin that is not the weakest; no flip point in tradeoff mode. |
| R8 | Style | Short active sentences, no hedges, one name per measure, no statistician's grammar above the fold. | Long or passive sentences dominate; hedges; two names for one measure; jargon above the fold. |
| R9 | The first screen | Masthead to options table alone say what to do, why, and the main risk. | Any of the three needs a section, the explore part or Method. |
| R10 | Next names the experiment that would change the answer | Next (What would settle it, in tradeoff mode) names a concrete experiment whose result could change the call, its decisive direction stated or clear from context. | A to-do list, "monitor" or "gather more data", an experiment that could not change the call, or one whose decisive direction is neither stated nor clear. |
| R11 | Each confidence clause says what would make its caveat material | Every clause names the condition under which its caveat would matter to the call, or that the deciding finding does not rest on it. No clauses: pass. | A clause that only restates the caveat, hedges, or names a condition that could not change the call. |
| R12 | Every figure supports its claim | Each figure in prose measures what its sentence says it does: a saving is a difference, a share is of what the sentence names, an arm's figure is that arm's, an interval is the one the claim is read on. | A figure attached to a claim it does not measure: "lowers cost by $1.47 per 1,000 replies" when $1.47 is the arm's cost, not the saving. |

## What a score record holds

One JSON file per plan scored, `<run_id>.scores.json` beside the plan: the run, the digests of its input and its plan,
the planner (model, provider, settings, prompt and contract digests), the scorer (`claude-opus-5-5`, or `owner` for a
human anchor), this rubric's version and digest, one entry per model-scored item (`id`, `verdict`, `reason`, `quote`,
`labeled_by`), and when it was scored. Scores pool only when the planner prompt digest, the rubric digest and the scorer
all match.
